                  BURNET COUNTY COMMISSIONERS COURT’S
              RESPONSE TO PRELIMARY ORDER ISSUE NOS. 11 AND 13



TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

       Burnet County Commissioners Court (“BCCC”) respectfully files Response on

Preliminary Order Issue Nos. 11 and 13 (Response) pursuant to State Office of Administrative

Hearing (“SOAH”) Order No. 35, which requires responses to initial briefing by October 19, 2026.

Therefore, this Response is timely filed.

       In Order No. 35, SOAH directed the parties, if they wished, to submit briefing on two

issues from the Public Utility Commission of Texas’s (“Commission”) Preliminary Order:

               11. Are the proposed transmission facilities necessary to meet state or federal

                   reliability standards; and




Burnet County Commissioners                                                            Page 1
Court’s Response to Preliminary Order Issues Nos. 11 and 13
                  13. What is the estimated congestion cost savings for consumers that may result

                     from the proposed transmission facilities considering both current and future

                     expected congestion levels and the ability of the proposed transmission

                     facilities to reduce those congestion levels?

Several parties filed briefs on those issues. The Order further set the deadline of October 19, 2026,

to respond to briefs filed on those issues. The Order did not reopen the evidentiary record.

       These issues were fully and properly addressed in SOAH’s Proposal For Decision, in

briefing and again by several intervenors in this docket in response to SOAH Order No. 35.

                                            Preliminary Issue No. 11

       BCCC agrees with Save Our Lampasas’s (“Lampasas”) Brief in Response to SOAH Order

No. 35 wherein they describe how the Joint Applicants failed to meet their burden of Proof with

regard the reliability need for this project.1 BCCC will not repeat similar arguments here. Because

Lampasas thoroughly argued these issues and included citations, BCCC adopts the Lampasas

arguments with citations in this Response.2

       The closed, record evidence decisively supports the SOAH PFD over the Joint Applicants

outdated studies. The SOAH ALJs should not change their answer to this issue as it is the

appropriate answer under this question.

                                            Preliminary Issue No. 13

       Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (“Oncor”) and LCRA Transmission Service

Corporation (“LCRA”), together the “Joint Applicants,” asserted at all times that their CCN




       1
           Save Our Lampasas Brief in Response to SOAH Order No. 35 at 4-7 (Oct. 7, 2026).
       2
           Id.
Burnet County Commissioners                                                                  Page 2
Court’s Response to Preliminary Order Issues Nos. 11 and 13
 application was a reliability project.3 The Joint Applicants have never asserted that the CCN was

an economic project, which is supported by their very general assertions of costs savings over the

ERCOT bulk network,4 rather than identifying congestion costs savings for consumers that may

result from the “proposed transmission facilities.”

       The SOAH Proposal for Decision (“PFD”) concluded that Oncor did not submit the

information necessary to answer Preliminary Issue No. 13,5 which Joint Applicants actually

acknowledged in their Initial Brief: “This Project is needed to address reliability issues and

establish additional load-serving capacity and is not justified based on economic criteria.”6 Now

Joint Applicants attempt to cobble together a different answer using pieces of generalized evidence

to assert that the Import 2 Path Projects will result in saving across some cost categories when

compared to a 345 kV alternative.7 That is not the appropriate comparison.

       Joint Applicants further use equivocal phrases such as “help resolve,”8 and “reduce the

need”9 exposing their failure to show congestion costs savings for Import Path 2, and even more

so for the Bell County East to Big Hill portion of Import Path 2. Joint Applicants’ continued

position that they are not required to demonstrate congestion costs savings because the Import Path

2 projects are reliability projects indicate that the SOAH ALJs should accept this position and

should not change their answer to this issue.10

Court’s Response to Preliminary Order Issues Nos. 11 and 13
                                             CONCLUSION

       There is nothing in the Joint Applicants’ Response to Order No. 35, nor in the closed

evidentiary record, that warrants any change in the PFD. BCCC, therefore, respectfully requests

that the SOAH ALJs keep their original recommendations in the PFD and find that the Joint

Application be denied, and for such other and further relief to which BCCC may be justly entitled.
